Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO): Implementation of 2027 GCTF Workshop in Eswatini Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) Implementation of 2027 G CTF Workshop in Eswatini American Institute in Taiwan Opportunity number: GCTF-TAIPEI-FY2 7 -00 1 Application deadline: November 23 , 202 6 , at 11:59 p.m. (Taipei Time)   A. Basic Information 1. Overview Funding Instrument Type: C ooperative agreement . Cooperative agreements include substantial involvement of the bureau or embassy in program implementation of the project. Examples of substantial involvement are included in section C.2 below. Project Performance Period : Proposed projects should be completed by May 31 , 202 7 . This notice is subject to availability of funding. The Public Diplomacy Section reserves the right to award less or more than the funds described under circumstances deemed to be in the best interest of the U.S. government, pending the availability of funds and approval of the designated grants officer. 2. Executive Summary The American Institute in Taiwan (AIT) Public Diplomacy Section (PDS) announces an open competition for a cooperative agreement to support the planning and implementation of a Global Cooperation and Training Framework (GCTF) regional franchise workshop in Eswatini in the first or second quarter of 2027. Subject to the availability of funding, AIT intends to award one cooperative agreement of approximately USD 200,000 to implement this program. The Global Cooperation and Training Framework (GCTF) is an international capacity-building platform that brings together government officials, technical experts, industry representatives, academics, and civil society representatives to exchange practical experiences and strengthen cooperation in addressing regional and global challenges. The GCTF was established by Taiwan and the United States in 2015 and has since expanded to include Japan, Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom as Partners. The proposed workshop, “Strengthening Cybersecurity and Digital Governance in Southern Africa,” is expected to take place in Eswatini during the first or second quarter of 2027. The program will focus on strengthening cybersecurity resilience, improving digital governance, protecting critical digital infrastructure, addressing emerging cyber threats, and promoting secure and trusted digital transformation. It will provide a platform for participants to exchange practical experiences, identify common challenges, and strengthen professional networks and regional cooperation. The workshop is expected to include representatives from at least eight African countries, with a particular emphasis on regional participation from Southern Africa. Approximately 60 to 80 participants are expected to participate in the first day of the program, which will feature plenary discussions, expert presentations, and practical exchanges. A smaller group of approximately 40 participants is expected to participate in the second day, which may include focused technical discussions, interactive exercises, working-group sessions, and/or relevant site visits. The program is expected to bring together government officials, cybersecurity and digital governance practitioners, technical experts, private-sector representatives, academics, civil society representatives, and other relevant stakeholders from participating African countries. Subject-matter experts from the United States, Taiwan, and other GCTF Partners, including Japan, Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom, may also be invited to contribute relevant international expertise and practical experience. The selected recipient will serve as AIT’s implementation partner and will be responsible for comprehensive program and logistical support, including venue and lodging coordination, participant management, travel arrangements for designated participants and speakers, ground transportation, interpretation and audiovisual services, workshop materials, vendor coordination, monitoring and evaluation, and required grant reporting. Travel expenses for U.S. Government officials invited by the U.S. Government and Taiwan-supported speakers will be funded separately and should not be included in the recipient’s proposed budget. AIT and GCTF partners will provide overall policy guidance, strategic direction, and substantive oversight throughout program planning and implementation. Eligible applicants include nonprofit organizations, educational institutions, professional associations, think tanks, private-sector organizations with relevant international program management experience, public international organizations where eligible under applicable U.S. Government regulations, and other eligible organizations with demonstrated capacity to organize international conferences or capacity-building programs and administer U.S. Government assistance awards. This cooperative agreement is intended to strengthen practical cybersecurity capacity and digital governance cooperation in Southern Africa, expand professional and institutional connections among participating countries, and advance the GCTF as a platform for practical international capacity building, technical exchange, and sustained regional cooperation. B. Eligibility 1. Eligible Applicants The following organizations are eligible to apply: Not-for-profit organizations , including non-governmental organizations (NGOs), think tanks, and civil society organizations Educational institutions , including universities and research institutions Professional associations and nonprofit organizations with demonstrated experience managing international conferences or capacity-building programs Private-sector organizations with demonstrated experience organizing international conferences or implementing international exchange programs Public international organizations , where eligible under applicable U.S. Government regulations Organizations may sub-contract with other entities, but only one entity, from the eligible categories of organizations listed above, can be the prime recipient of the award. When sub-contracting with other entities, the responsibilities of each entity must be clearly defined in the proposal. For more information on the difference between sub-contract and sub-recipient, please refer to 2 CFR 200 .331 . 2. Cost Sharing or Matching Cost sharing is not required . 3. Other Eligibility Requirements All organizations must have a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) issued via SAM.gov as well as a valid registration in SAM.gov. Please see Section D.3 for more information. Individuals are not required to have a UEI or be registered in SAM.gov. Applicants are only allowed to submit one proposal per organization. If more than one proposal is submitted from an organization, all proposals from that institution will be considered ineligible for funding. 4. This opportunity will not support: Projects relating to partisan political activity; Charitable or development activities; including direct social services such as medical, psychological, and/or humanitarian support Construction projects; Projects that support specific religious activities; Fund-raising campaigns; Lobbying for specific legislation or programs Scientific research or surveys; Commercial projects; Projects intended primarily for the growth or institutional development of the organization; Projects that duplicate existing projects; Illegal activities C. Program Description 1. Project Background, Goals, and Objectives Project Background The Global Cooperation and Training Framework (GCTF) is an international capacity-building platform established by Taiwan and the United States in 2015. Japan joined as a full partner in 2019, followed by Australia in 2021, Canada in 2023, and the United Kingdom in 2025. Through workshops and other capacity-building activities, GCTF brings together government officials, technical experts, industry representatives, and civil society representatives to exchange practical experience, strengthen professional networks, and develop approaches to shared regional and global challenges. As governments and societies become increasingly dependent on digital technologies and interconnected systems, cybersecurity and effective digital governance have become important elements of economic development, public-service delivery, critical infrastructure resilience, and public trust. Recent research documents that scam syndicates displaced from Southeast Asian epicenters, including Myanmar, Laos, and Cambodia, are actively pivoting to Africa, with documented raids in nine African countries and growing evidence of scam infrastructure, including online gambling platforms used as cover for fraud operations, gray business Telegram groups openly advertising scam facilities, and unregulated cryptocurrency services establishing footholds across the continent. Countries across Southern Africa face evolving cybersecurity and cybercrime challenges while also seeking to expand digital services, strengthen institutional capacity, and develop governance frameworks that support secure and trusted digital transformation. The proposed GCTF regional workshop in Eswatini will provide a platform for government officials, cybersecurity and the digital governance practitioners, technical experts, private-sector representatives, academics, civil society representatives, and other relevant stakeholders from across Africa to exchange practical experiences and strengthen professional and institutional connections. The workshop is expected to include representatives from at least eight African countries, with particular emphasis on participation from Southern Africa. The program will draw on expertise and practical experience from participating African countries as well as the United States, Taiwan, and other GCTF partners, as appropriate. Through expert presentations, policy and technical discussions, interactive exchanges, and other practical activities, the workshop will address shared challenges and identify approaches that participating countries may adapt to their respective national and institutional contexts. Strengthening cybersecurity capacity and secure digital governance in Southern Africa also advances U.S. security and economic interests. Cyber threats, cyber-enabled crime, and vulnerabilities in interconnected digital systems increasingly cross-national borders and can affect American citizens, businesses, and critical infrastructure. By strengthening the ability of partner countries to prevent, identify, respond to, and recover from cyber threats, this program can help reduce vulnerabilities that may be exploited by transnational criminal networks and other malicious cyber actors. The workshop will also strengthen U.S. engagement with African partners on secure and resilient digital ecosystems, promote cooperation and information sharing among governments and technical experts, and expand relationships between African stakeholders and the United States and other GCTF partners. Through practical capacity building and sustained professional networks, the program will support a more secure and resilient regional digital environment while advancing shared interests in cybersecurity, economic security, and trusted digital development. Project Goal: The goal of this project is to strengthen cybersecurity resilience and digital governance capacity in Southern Africa by facilitating practical knowledge exchange, regional cooperation, and sustained professional engagement among participating countries and international partners, while advancing shared U.S. and partner interests in a more secure, resilient, and trusted digital environment. Project Objectives: The project will pursue the following objectives: Strengthen Cybersecurity Capacity and Resilience: Enhance participants’ knowledge of practical approaches to preventing, preparing for, responding to, and recovering from cybersecurity threats and incidents, with a specific focus on basic cyber hygiene, national cyber resilience, digital trust, and the development of a secure digital ecosystem aligned with global standards and best practices. Advance Effective and Secure Digital Governance: Promote the exchange of policies, practices, institutional approaches, and lessons learned that support secure, trusted, resilient, and inclusive digital governance and digital transformation. Promote Regional Cooperation and Information Sharing: Strengthen professional and institutional connections among participating African countries and encourage greater cross-border cooperation, information sharing, and coordination in addressing shared cybersecurity and digital governance challenges. Facilitate Practical International Exchange: Connect African policymakers and practitioners with relevant expertise and practical experience from participating African countries, the United States, Taiwan, and other GCTF partner countries, including Japan, Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom, as appropriate to the workshop agenda. Support Sustainable Professional Networks and Follow-on Cooperation: Encourage participants to identify practical opportunities for continued professional engagement, knowledge sharing, and future cooperation beyond the workshop. 2. Substantial Involvement This award will require substantial involvement from the American Institute in Taiwan (AIT ) and the U . S . Embassy in Eswatini . AIT will approve all key aspects of the workshop, including but not limited to venue selection, flight and hotel arrangements, ground transportation, lodging, visual designs, agenda, site visit locations, speaker and participant lists, catering and menus, conference room layout, lighting, and audio-visual setup. D. Application Contents and Format Please follow all instructions below carefully. Proposals that do not meet the requirements of this announcement or fail to comply with the stated requirements will be ineligible. Content of Application Please ensure: The proposal clearly addresses the goals and objectives of this funding opportunity All documents are in English All budgets are in U.S. dollars All pages are numbered, including budgets and attachments All documents are formatted to fit 8 ½ x 11 paper All documents are single-spaced, 14-point New Times Roman font, with 1-inch margins. Captions and footnotes may be 10-point New Times Roman font. Font sizes in charts and tables, including the budget, can be reformatted to fit within 1 page width. All applicant authorized signatures are provided where indicated on the various, required forms. The following documents are required: 1. Mandatory application forms SF-424 (Application for Federal Assistance – organizations) at https://grants.gov/ or https://www.ait.org.tw / . SF-424A (Budget Information for Non-Construction programs) at https://grants.gov/ or https://www.ait.org.tw / . SF-424B (Assurances for Non-Construction programs) at https://grants.gov/ or https://www.ait.org.tw / . (note: the SF-424B is only required for individuals, organizations exempt from registration, and for organizations not required to fully register in https://sam.gov/ ) 2. Proposal (10 pages maximum) The proposal should contain sufficient information that anyone not familiar with it would understand exactly what the applicant wants to do. You may use your own proposal format, but it must include all the items below. Proposal Summary: Short narrative that outlines the proposed project, including project objectives and anticipated impact. (Attachment: Recommended Proposal Template ). Introduction to the Organization : A description of past and present operations, showing ability to carry out the program, including information on all previous grants from the State Department and/or U.S. government agencies as well as experience with and expertise in areas related to those described in the NOFO. Applicants are encouraged, but not required, to use the attached Applicant Organization Information Survey form to provide this information (Attachment : Recommended Applicant Organization Information (AOI) Survey Template ). If the applicant chooses not to use the attached form, all of the requested information from the form will still need to be addressed in the application package. Problem Statement: Clear, concise and well-supported statement of the problem to be addressed and why the proposed program is needed Program Methods, Design, Activities, and Deliverables: The “goals” describe what the program is intended to achieve. The “objectives” refer to the intermediate accomplishments on the way to the goals. These should be achievable and measurable. Describe the program activities and how they will help achieve the objectives. Proposed Project Schedule and Timeline: The proposed timeline for the program activities. Include the dates, times, and locations of planned activities and events. Key Personnel: Names, titles, roles and experience/qualifications of key personnel involved in the program. What proportion of their time will be used in support of this program? Project Partners: List the names and type of involvement of key partner organizations and sub-awardees (if applicable). Future Funding or Sustainability: Applicant’s plan for continuing the program beyond the grant period, or the availability of other resources, if applicable. Monitoring & Evaluation Plan: Proposals must include a draft Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Performance Monitoring Plan (PMP). The M&E PMP should show how applicants intend to measure and demonstrate progress towards the project’s objectives and goals. The key components to the PMP are as follows: Monitoring and Evaluation Narrative: In narrative form, applicants should describe how they intend to monitor and evaluate the activities of their award. In addition, the applicant should describe any M&E processes, including key personnel, management structure (where M&E fits into the overall program’s staff structure), technology, and as well provide a brief budget narrative explaining any line-item expenditures for M&E listed in the program’s budget. If the proposal is from a prior grantee, the proposal discusses how the grantee has adapted, improved or otherwise modified their approach based on learning from previous experience. This narrative is limited to two pages. Theory of Change Diagram: Applicants are expected to submit either a Theory of Change diagram or an If-Then Statement that illustrates how project activities will lead to intended outcomes. Monitoring and Evaluation Datasheet: The applicant must include their proposed activities and their expected outputs and outcomes as well as the goals and objectives as written in the NOFO. The datasheet’s purpose is to explicitly illustrate how a project’s activities lead to tangible results (such as increased beneficiary skills, knowledge, or attitudes) that ultimately address a PDS objective. The selected applicant’s M&E PMP is subject to review and approval before any award will be issued under this NOFO. The selected applicant will be required to work with the Public Diplomacy Section’s Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist to ensure the applicant’s M&E PMP achieves an expected level of expertise and meets PDS objectives. Expenses directly associated with monitoring and evaluation are considered allowable. The suggested template includes a space to list the portion of the total budget amount directly associated with monitoring and evaluation activities. 3. Budget Justification Narrative Detailed Budget – Applicants must submit a detailed line-item budget. Applicants are encouraged to utilize the template provided with the funding opportunity but are not required to do so (Attachment: Recommended Budget Narrative Template ). Line-item expenditures should be listed in the greatest possible detail. The budget must identify the total amount of funding requested, with a breakdown of amounts to be spent in the following budget categories: personnel; fringe benefits; travel; equipment; supplies; consultants/contracts; other direct costs; and indirect costs. See Annex Section I for a description of the types of costs that should be included in each category. Personnel salaries should include the level of effort and the rate of pay, which should cover the percentage of time each staff member will dedicate to grant-based activities. If an organization is charging an indirect cost rate without a NICRA, it must apply it to the modified total budget costs (MTDC), refer to 2CFR § 200.1 . Budgets shall be submitted in U.S. dollars and final grant agreements will be conducted in U.S. dollars. Budget Justification Narrative – Applicants must submit a budget justification narrative to accompany the detailed line-item budget. The purpose of the budget justification narrative is to supplement the information provided in the detailed budget spreadsheet by justifying how the budget cost elements are necessary to implement project objectives and accomplish the project goals. The budget justification narrative is a tool to help AIT staff fully understand the budgetary needs of the applicant and is an opportunity to provide descriptive information about the requested costs beyond the constraints of the budget template. Together, the detailed budget spreadsheet, the budget justification narrative, and the SF-424A should provide a complete financial and qualitative description that supports the proposed project plan and should be directly relatable to the specific project components described in the applicant’s proposal. Additional Budget Notes: Curing venues, managing logistics, catering, etc. are allowable. Audit Requirements: Please note the audit requirements for Department of State awards in the Standard Terms and Conditions https://www.state.gov/federal-assistance-policies-appeals, Subpart F – Audit Requirements. The cost of the required audits may be charged either as an allowable direct cost to the award OR included in the organization’s established indirect costs in the award’s detailed budget. Visa Fees: Include all visa application and related fees in your budget as applicable. Please note DS-2019s for post-funded programs must be submitted directly by the award recipient. If you anticipate your program will include the DS-2019 visa processing, your organization must be a registered Designated Sponsoring Organization. For more information go to: https://j1visa.state.gov/sponsors/become-a-sponsor/ 4. Attachments Key Personnel Resumes : A résumé, not to exceed one page in length, must be included for the proposed key staff persons, such as the Project Director and Finance Officer, as well as any speakers or trainers (if applicable). If an individual for this type of position has not been identified, the applicant may submit a 1-page position description, identifying the qualifications and skills required for that position, in lieu of a résumé. Letters of support from program partners: Letters of support should be included for sub-recipients or other partners. The letters must identify the type of relationship to be entered into (formal or informal), the roles and responsibilities of each partner in relation to the proposed project activities, and the expected result of the partnership. The individual letters cannot exceed 1 page in length. Indirect Costs : If your organization has a Negotiated Indirect Cost Rate Agreement (NICRA) and includes NICRA charges in the budget, your latest NICRA should be included in the application submission. Proof of Non-profit Status: Documentation to demonstrate the applicant’s non-profit status (e.g., U.S.-based organizations should submit a copy of their 501(c)(3) Internal Revenue Service determination letter, and non-U.S. organizations should provide evidence of non-profit status issued by a government entity). Proof of Registration: A copy of the organization’s registration should be provided with the proposal application. U.S.-based organizations should submit a copy of their IRS determination letter. Taiwan -based organizations should submit a copy of their certificate of registration from the appropriate government organization. Other items NOT required/requested with the application submission, but which may be requested if your application is approved to move forward in the review process include: Copies of an organization or program audit within the last two (2) years Copies of relevant human resources, financial, or procurement policies Copies of other relevant organizational policies or documentation that would help the Department determine your organization’s capacity to manage a federal grant award overseas Documentation that demonstrates the recipients’ plan and/or policy to safeguard PII of participants and beneficiaries. It is the responsibility of the recipient to ensure protection of personally identifiable information (PII) and safeguard PII when collecting, maintaining, using and disseminating such information Information to determine what financial controls and standard operating procedures an organization uses to procure goods and services, hire staff and track time and attendance, pay for grant-related travel, and identify other financial transactions that may be necessary to undertake the project activities AIT reserves the right to request any additional programmatic and/or financial information regarding the proposal. Review Criteria Criteria: Each application submitted under this announcement will be evaluated and rated on the basis of the criteria enumerated below. The criteria are designed to assess the quality of the proposed project, and to determine the likelihood of its success. Quality and Feasibility of the Program Idea – 20 points: The program idea should be innovative and well developed, with sufficient detail about how p roject activities will be carried out. The proposals should demonstrate originality and outline clear, achievable objectives that align directly with the priorities and requirements of the NOFO . The proposal includes a reasonable implementation timeline, and the project scope is appropriate and clearly defined. Finally, the proposal aligns with the following: The project clearly demonstrates a direct contribution to current U.S. foreign policy priorities. The project will positively impact America’s reputation among foreign government partners. The project will positively impact American’s reputation among foreign publics. The proposal does not include any activities contrary to the following Executive Orders: Executive Order 14173: “Ending Illegal Discrimination and Restoring Merit-Based Opportunity Executive Order 14287: “Protecting American Communities from Criminal Aliens” Executive Order 14168: Defending Women from Gender Ideology Extremism and Restoring Biological Truth to the Federal Government Organizational Capacity and Record on Previous Grants – 20 points: The project proposal demonstrates that the organization has sufficient expertise, skills, and human resources to implement the project, including internal contr ols in place to manage federal funds. The organization demonstrates that it has a clear understanding of the underlying issue that the project will address. The organization demonstrates capacity for successful planning and responsible fiscal management. This includes a financial management system , a bank account , and if applicable, satisfactory audit findings. Applicants who have received grant funds previously have been compliant with applicable rules and regulations , including the Award Provisions and Standard Terms and Conditions. Where partners are described, the applicant details each partner’s respective role and provides curriculum vitae (CVs) for persons responsible for the project and financial administration. Proposed personnel, institutional resources, and partners are adequate and appropriate. Project Planning/Ability to Achieve Objectives – 25 points: The project plan is well developed, with sufficient detail about how activities will be carried out. The proposal specifies target audiences, participant recruitment, and geographic areas of implementation. The proposal outlines clear, achievable objectives. The proposal includes a reasonable implementation timeline. The project scope is appropriate and clearly defined. Budget – 15 points: The budget and narrative justification are sufficiently detailed. The budget demonstrates that the organization has devoted time to accurately determine expenses associated with the project instead of providing rough estimates. Costs are reasonable in relation to the proposed activities and anticipated results. The results and proposed outcomes justify the total cost of the project. Budget items are reasonable, allowable, and allocable. Monitoring and Evaluation – 10 points: There is a complete and thorough draft submission of a M&E Performance Monitoring Plan (PMP). This will include a list of proposed project activities, corresponding milestone, output, and outcome indicators, a description of data collection methods, and a timeline for collecting such information. The proposal presents a clear theory of change on how the program will address that problem. Funded projects will have their plans finalized during the negotiation phase, and monitoring plans may be subject to periodic updates throughout the life of the project. Sustainability – 10 points: The project proposal describes clearly the approach that will be used to ensure maximum sustainability or advancement of project goals after the end of project activity. 2. Travel: Estimate the costs of travel and per diem for this program, for program staff, consultants or speakers, and participants/beneficiaries. If the program involves international travel, include a brief statement of justification for that travel. Equipment: Describe any machinery, furniture, or other personal property that is required for the program, which has a useful life of more than one year (or a life longer than the duration of the program), and costs at least $10,000 per unit. Supplies: List and describe all the items and materials, including any computer devices, that are needed for the program. If an item costs more than $10,000 per unit, then put it in the budget under Equipment. Contractual: Describe goods and services that the applicant plans to acquire through a contract with a vendor. Also describe any sub-awards to non-profit partners that will help carry out the program activities. Other Direct Costs: Describe other costs directly associated with the program, which do not fit in the other categories. For example, shipping costs for materials and equipment or applicable taxes. All “Other” or “Miscellaneous” expenses must be itemized and explained. Indirect Costs: These are costs that cannot be linked directly to the program activities, such as overhead costs needed to help keep the organization operating. If your organization has a Negotiated Indirect Cost Rate (NICRA) and includes NICRA charges in the budget, attach a copy of your latest NICRA. Organizations that have never had a NICRA may request indirect costs of 15% of Modified Total Direct Costs (MTDC) as defined in 2 CFR 200.1. “Cost Sharing” refers to contributions from the organization or other entities other than AIT. It also includes in-kind contributions such as volunteers’ time and donated venues. 内容摘要：中华人民共和国 (PRC) 正在扩大对 RISC-V（一种开源芯片设计标准）的使用，并扩大其对管理该标准的国际非营利组织的影响力。近年来，人们越来越担心被切断与 Arm 和英特尔等西方行业领导者设计的芯片的联系。中国公司现在不仅为消费设备而且为服务器和数据中心制造 RISC-V 芯片，尽管它们的功能不如专有芯片。 V100于10月推出，由国家支持的实体共同创建，号称是首款完全符合RISC-V服务器标准的通用芯片。国家级政策文件传统上避免直接讨论RISC-V，但今年9月，《电子信息制造业“十五五”规划》宣布，要求推进RISC-V研发和产业化，开发人工智能（AI）RISC-V芯片。 RISC-V 为自力更生带来了明显的好处，并且芯片可以进行调整，包括针对军事用例进行优化。
然而，中国的分析师担心芯片的“玻璃天花板”，甚至国家 IT 替代计划也指出，在政府系统中用于替代外国技术的 RISC-V 芯片的份额“可以忽略不计”。 10月19日，深圳芯片制造商进迭时空与香山处理器团队在第六届RISC-V中国峰会上推出了新型46核服务器芯片V100。[1]其制造商宣称其是首款完全符合RISC-V服务器标准的通用芯片（21世纪经济报道，10月19日；科技日报，10月20日）。 RISC-V 是一种开源指令集架构 (ISA)，是处理器运行的语言。与全球几乎所有计算机和手机中使用的 Arm 或 Intel x86 等专有 ISA 不同，任何人都可以使用 RISC-V，无需支付许可费或需要其他权限。由英国和美国公司制造的 Arm 和英特尔处理器必须遵守这些国家政府实施的许可和出口管制。相比之下，RISC-V 主要由 RISC-V International 监管，这是一家总部位于瑞士的非营利组织，旨在避免此类漏洞。最近推出的服务器芯片代表了中华人民共和国（PRC）该行业更广泛的趋势。
北京最初在 2010 年代中期开始将 RISC-V 视为对抗西方技术霸权并扩大其在新兴技术领域结构性力量的一种方式（中国简报，2023 年 12 月 15 日）。此后，北京通过国家主导的政策支持鼓励其发展，从城市层面开始，逐步上升到国家层面。尽管这些芯片的功能仍然落后于西方竞争对手，但它们越来越多地部署在数据中心的服务器中，而不仅仅是嵌入消费设备中。从市政厅到五年计划 2023年以来，地方层面对RISC-V的支持已经明确，特别是在上海、北京和深圳等一线城市（中国简报，2023年12月15日）。北京经济技术开发区的目标是到 2030 年使 RISC-V 产业价值超过 500 亿元人民币（70 亿美元），据一些估计，届时全国市场将达到约 2200 亿元人民币（210 亿美元）（北京市政府，2025 年 1 月 3 日；中国日报）

【原文 English Original】
Executive Summary: The People’s Republic of China (PRC) is expanding its use of RISC-V, an open-source chip design standard, as well as its influence over the international nonprofit organization that manages it. This follows growing fears in recent years of being cut off from chips designed by Western industry leaders such as Arm and Intel. PRC firms are now creating RISC-V chips not just for consumer devices but for servers and data centers, even though they are less powerful than proprietary chips. The V100, launched in October and co-created by a state-backed entity, is billed as the first general-purpose chip fully compliant with RISC-V server standards. National-level policy documents have traditionally avoided discussing RISC-V directly, but in September, the 15th Five-Year Plan for the Electronic Information Manufacturing Industry announced calls to advance RISC-V research, development, and industrialization, and to develop RISC-V chips for artificial intelligence (AI). RISC-V brings clear benefits for self-reliance, and the chips can be adapted, including being optimized for military use cases. Analysts in the PRC worry, however, about a “glass ceiling” for the chips, and even the state IT substitution program has noted that the share of RISC-V chips it has used to replace foreign technology in government systems is “negligible.” On October 19, Shenzhen-based chipmaker SpacemiT (进迭时空) and the state-backed XiangShan (香山) processor team launched the V100, a new 46-core server chip, at the sixth RISC-V Summit China.  [1] Its makers bill it as the first general-purpose chip fully compliant with RISC-V server standards ( 21st Century Business Herald , October 19; Science and Technology Daily , October 20). RISC-V is an open-source instruction set architecture (ISA), which is the language that processors run on. Unlike proprietary ISAs, such as Arm or Intel’s x86 that are used in almost all of the world’s computers and phones, anyone can use RISC-V without paying a license fee or requiring other permissions. Arm and Intel processors, made by British and U.S. companies, must abide by licensing and export controls put in place by those countries’ governments. By comparison, RISC-V is mainly overseen by RISC-V International, a Switzerland-based nonprofit that avoids such vulnerabilities. The recently unveiled server chip is representative of broader trends in the sector within the People’s Republic of China (PRC). Beijing initially began to view RISC-V as a way to counter the West’s technological hegemony and extend its structural power in emerging technologies in the mid-2010s ( China Brief , December 15, 2023). Since then, it has encouraged its development through state-led policy support, starting at the city level and moving up to the national level. Although the chips’ capabilities remain behind those of Western rivals, they are increasingly being deployed in servers for data centers, not just embedded in consumer devices. From City Halls to the Five-Year Plan Since 2023, local-level support for RISC-V has been explicit, especially in first-tier cities like Shanghai, Beijing, and Shenzhen ( China Brief , December 15, 2023). Beijing’s Economic-Technological Development Area aims for a RISC-V industry worth more than renminbi (RMB) 50 billion ($7 billion) by 2030, at which point the national market will reach around RMB 220 billion ($21 billion), according to some estimates ( Beijing Municipal Government , January 3, 2025; China Daily , October 22). National-level documents have tended instead to use the term “open source” to implicitly refer to RISC-V. In mid-September, however, the 15th Five-Year Plan for the Electronic Information Manufacturing Industry announced calls to “advance the research, development, and industrialization of RISC-V” (推进第五代精简指令集 (RISC-V) 研发与产业化), and to support RISC-V artificial intelligence (AI) and embedded system chips ( Ministry of Information and Industry Technology , September 15).  [2] Server Ambitions, Smartphone-Class Silicon RISC-V’s strength so far has been in cheaper control chips for appliances and cars, but newer chips signal data center servers as an emerging use case. The Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) calls the open-source XiangShan core the most powerful of its kind in the world ( China Daily , March 26). Beyond the latest processor from SpacemiT and XiangShan, Alibaba now offers a server-class design, the C950, that it says performs on par with Apple’s M1 chip, which it released in 2020, on a standard performance test ( The Register , March 25). Engineers usually judge how well a core is designed via a two-step process. First, they run an industry-standard test, which times how long a processor takes to complete a set of tasks, and turns that time into a score. Second, they divide the score by the core’s clock speed, which is the number of steps it takes each second, measured in gigahertz (GHz). The result measures how much work a core does in each step (see Figure 1). On this metric, PRC progress is substantial: XiangShan’s cores have roughly doubled since 2021. In an independent test run on SpacemiT’s most recently commercially produced desktop and edge chip showed it as running slightly slower than the U.K.-designed Raspberry Pi 5 hobby computer, which was released in 2023 ( CNX Software , January 23). The speed that a core runs matters too, as a chip with a well-designed core may still lose out in the long term to a more basic chip whose core has a faster clock speed. Measured at the speeds they actually run, the best cores in the SpacemiT/XiangShan processor are well behind Nvidia’s leading Grace server processor, and those produced by Arm and Intel (see Figure 2). Alibaba’s C950, which it licenses to other chipmakers, comes close to or beats Grace based on the firm’s internal testing. RISC-V Buys Assurance and Customization RISC-V offers the PRC with two benefits: the assurance of sustainable access, and adaptability for military purposes, which would be risky use-cases for employing Western chips. The fear of being cut off from access to chips has been acute since Huawei learned in 2019 that its access to Arm’s designs could be suspended ( BBC , May 22, 2019). As an open-source architecture, RISC-V can be modified and tailored to user requirements. In some instances, however, this has allowed it to be adapted for military purposes. A team at Information Engineering University, an institution affiliated with the People’s Liberation Army, was able to customize command for data encryption to a small RISC-V chip, accelerating encryption by about seven times with only about two percent more circuitry.  [5] These benefits are another part of the reason why the PRC has pushed to deepen its influence over RISC-V at the international level. Chinese firms now hold half of the 24 top-tier memberships in RISC-V International ( RISC-V , accessed November 3). U.S. firms are deepening their stake in the RISC-V ecosystem too. Nvidia said in July 2025 that its CUDA software, the backbone of AI computing, would support RISC-V processors, and Qualcomm bought the RISC-V server designer Ventana in December 2025 ( The Register , July 21, 2025; Qualcomm , December 10, 2025). Conclusion Beijing continues to emphasize RISC-V to advance technological self-reliance and resilience. Although it is starting to use RISC-V chips in servers and data centers, the chips function at well below the capabilities of the most advanced processors. Analysts in the PRC have worried about a “glass ceiling” (玻璃天花板) for the chips, and even the state IT substitution program (信创) has noted that the share of RISC-V chips it has used to replace foreign technology in government systems is “negligible (微乎其微)” ( Sina Finance , April 7). It is nevertheless too soon to dismiss the hype over the PRC’s RISC-V development. RISC-V currently also enjoys support from U.S. companies. This makes the international standards that govern RISC-V an important battle ground in the competition to shape this arena of open-source technology. It remains unclear, however, whether the United States will seek to build a U.S.-led ISA ecosystem or discourage U.S. and allied firms from taking part in Chinese-led RISC-V projects. Neither option is cost-free, although if Washington does not take action, a key part of the semiconductor supply chain could end up being controlled by Beijing. Notes [1] A core is the part of a processor that reads and carries out software instructions. [2] The plan was released by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) and the National Development and Reform Commission, but grew out of work by eight agencies that drafted the country’s first national guidance on RISC-V in 2025 ( Reuters , March 3, 2025). [3] For Figure 2, panel A estimates the real speed of a single core by multiplying its points per gigahertz by the clock speed at which it actually ships, and shows the result relative to a core in Nvidia’s Grace server processor (set at 100). Intel and AMD do not publish comparable SPECint2006 figures, so their desktop cores are set equal to Arm’s Cortex-X925, which independent testing by Chips and Cheese found to be within the margin of error of the fastest AMD and Intel cores on the newer SPECint2017 test ( Chips and Cheese, March 3 ). Panels B and C compare whole server chips. The first is the number of cores. Each core works on its own task, so more cores means more work at once. The second is memory speed, or bandwidth: how many gigabytes of data a chip can move to and from its memory each second. In large data-center jobs this is often the real limit, because even a fast core sits idle while it waits for data. The lower panels of Figure 2 compare other measures of performance for entire server chips. The V100 has 46 cores; Nvidia’s Grace has 72; and the top Intel and AMD server chips have 128–192. The V100 also moves data to and from memory at about half their speed. It draws far less power, however, at 120 watts, compared to about 250 for Grace and 500 for the Intel and AMD chips ( GitHub , accessed October 27). [4] Figure 3 measures AI performance in trillions of simple calculations per second (TOPS). Since AI models run on vast numbers of such calculations, higher TOPS values translate to faster AI. The left panel divides TOPS by the power a chip draws, in watts, to show energy efficiency, which matters most in battery-powered robots and drones. The right panel shows raw TOPS for laptop chips. Companies quote TOPS in different ways that can double or even quadruple the headline number, so the chart puts every chip on the same basis. Even if the SpacemiT processor reaches 30 TOPS, this is still short of Microsoft’s bar of 40. By The Register’s estimate, even Alibaba’s best design would roughly match Apple’s M1 ( The Register , March 25). [5] Zhang Xiaolei, Dai Zibin, Guo Pengfei, et al., “Design and Verification of a RISC-V-Based AES Cryptographic Acceleration Engine [基于RISC-V的AES密码加速引擎设计与验证],” Application of Electronic Technique [电子技术应用] 49, no. 2 (2023): 39–44. Results are from FPGA prototypes built on the open-source Hummingbird E203 core. The post RISC-V Open-Source Chip Push Puts Strategy Over Capability appeared first on Jamestown .

title: Update Chrome now to fix a flaw attackers are exploiting
zh_title: 立即更新 Chrome 以修复攻击者利用的漏洞
summary: 11 月 9 日，谷歌发布了适用于 Windows、Mac 和 Linux 的 Chrome 稳定频道的安全更新。该更新将在未来几天和几周内推出。大多数用户都使用 Chrome 的稳定渠道。此次桌面更新将 Chrome 带到了 Windows 和 Mac 版本 157.0.8103.50/.51 以及 Linux 版本 157.0.8103.50。它包括九个安全修复程序，其中一个针对被积极利用的零日漏洞。零日漏洞是在官方修复可用之前披露或利用的安全缺陷。香港计算机紧急应变小组协调中心（HKCERT）
content:
11 月 9 日，谷歌发布了适用于 Windows、Mac 和 Linux 的 Chrome 稳定频道的安全更新。该更新将在未来几天和几周内推出。大多数用户都使用 Chrome 的稳定渠道。此次桌面更新将 Chrome 带到了 Windows 和 Mac 版本 157.0.8103.50/.51 以及 Linux 版本 157.0.8103.50。它包括九个安全修复程序，其中一个针对被积极利用的零日漏洞。零日漏洞是在官方修复可用之前披露或利用的安全缺陷。香港计算机应急响应小组协调中心（HKCERT）将总体风险评级为“极高”。其公告称，更新中解决的一些漏洞可能允许拒绝服务、安全限制绕过和远程代码执行。如何更新 Chrome 最简单的选择是允许 Chrome 自动更新。但是，如果您从未关闭浏览器或出现问题（例如扩展程序阻止更新），您最终可能会落后于更新。如果您不想等待发布，您可以手动更新。从 Chrome 的“设置”或“帮助”菜单中打开“关于 Google Chrome”。 Chrome 将检查更新并下载任何可用的更新。如果出现提示，请单击“重新启动”以应用它。 Chrome 157.0.8103.51 已更新 您可以在我们的指南中找到版本编号系统的说明和分步说明：如何在每个操作系统上更新 Chrome 。
谷歌还于 11 月 9 日发布了 Android 版 Chrome 157.0.8103.50。谷歌表示，除非另有说明，否则它包含与桌面版本相同的安全修复程序。 Android 用户应检查 Google Play 是否有更新。技术细节让我们仔细看看这个零日漏洞。谷歌表示，它于 11 月 6 日收到未具名第三方的漏洞通知。该漏洞被追踪为 CVE-2026-125350，并被评为 Chrome XML 组件中的高严重性释放后使用漏洞。 XML 是 Chrome 用来读取和处理某些类型的结构化 Web 内容的数据格式。 XML 代表可扩展标记语言：它使用标签来标记信息，就像 HTML 一样，但允许作者定义自己的标签来描述他们的数据。当程序尝试访问已释放的内存位置时，就会发生释放后使用漏洞。这可能会导致崩溃，或者在某些情况下，允许攻击者运行自己的代码。谷歌仅表示“意识到 CVE-2026-125350 的漏洞存在”。它没有透露攻击者、目标、交付方法或该漏洞可以做什么。在威胁造成任何伤害之前阻止它们。 Malwarebytes Browser Guard 自动阻止网络钓鱼页面和恶意网站。免费，一键安装。将其添加到您的浏览器 →

【原文 English Original】
On November 9, Google issued a security update to Chrome’s Stable channel for Windows, Mac, and Linux. The update is rolling out over the coming days and weeks. Most users are on Chrome’s Stable channel. The desktop update brings Chrome to versions 157.0.8103.50/.51 for Windows and Mac and 157.0.8103.50 for Linux . It includes nine security fixes, including one for an actively exploited zero-day vulnerability. A zero-day vulnerability is a security flaw disclosed or exploited before an official fix becomes available. Hong Kong’s Computer Emergency Response Team Coordination Centre (HKCERT) rates the overall risk as “Extremely High.” Its bulletin says some of the vulnerabilities address in the update could allow denial of service, security restriction bypass, and remote code execution. How to update Chrome The easiest option is to allow Chrome to update automatically. But you can end up lagging behind on updates if you never close your browser or if something goes wrong, such as an extension preventing the update. If you don’t want to wait for the rollout to reach you, you can update manually. Open About Google Chrome from Chrome’s Settings or Help menu. Chrome will check for updates and download any available update. If prompted, click Relaunch to apply it. Chrome 157.0.8103.51 is up to date You can find an explanation of the version numbering system and step-by-step instructions in our guide: How to update Chrome on every operating system . Google also released Chrome 157.0.8103.50 for Android on November 9. Google says it includes the same security fixes as the desktop release unless otherwise noted. Android users should check Google Play for the update. Technical details Let’s take a closer look at that zero-day vulnerability. Google says it was notified about a vulnerability by an unnamed third party on November 6. The vulnerability is tracked as CVE-2026-125350 and rated as a high-severity use-after-free vulnerability in Chrome’s XML component. XML is a data format Chrome uses to read and process certain kinds of structured web content. XML stands for Extensible Markup Language: it labels information with tags, rather like HTML, but allows authors to define their own tags to describe their data. A use-after-free vulnerability occurs when a program attempts to access a memory location after it has been freed. That can cause crashes or, in some cases, allow an attacker to run their own code. Google only says that it is “aware that an exploit for CVE-2026-125350 exists in the wild.” It has not named the attackers, the targets, the delivery method, or what the exploit can do. title: 特朗普称下周或与习近平、普京在中国举行三方会谈
summary: 特朗普向记者表示，他将前往中国，并预计与习近平及普京会面。他说：“我将前往中国，而我认为其中一场会议将会是与普京总统及习近平主席举行，这将会很有意思。”他又表示，会谈将涉及多项议题，包括核裁军及结束伊朗战争。 中国外交部发言人毛宁表示，中方正与有关方面就三国元首会晤保持沟通。俄罗斯克里姆林宫发言人佩斯科夫（Dmitry Peskov）证实，相关协调工作正在进行，希望未来数日内敲定安排。他说：“我们希望能在未来几天内敲定这件事。” 克里姆林宫早于10月21日已表示，三方会谈正在
content: 特朗普向记者表示，他将前往中国，并预计与习近平及普京会面。他说：“我将前往中国，而我认为其中一场会议将会是与普京总统及习近平主席举行，这将会很有意思。”他又表示，会谈将涉及多项议题，包括核裁军及结束伊朗战争。 中国外交部发言人毛宁表示，中方正与有关方面就三国元首会晤保持沟通。俄罗斯克里姆林宫发言人佩斯科夫（Dmitry Peskov）证实，相关协调工作正在进行，希望未来数日内敲定安排。他说：“我们希望能在未来几天内敲定这件事。” 克里姆林宫早于10月21日已表示，三方会谈正在筹备。美国《华尔街日报》此前报道，普京希望透过会谈促成乌克兰和平协议，争取对莫斯科有利的安排。俄罗斯自2022年全面入侵乌克兰后，一直面对西方国家的外交孤立及制裁。 分析人士指出，普京可能是这场会谈的最大受益者。即使三方未能达成协议，只要普京能与特朗普及习近平同场亮相，已可向外界展示俄罗斯仍是国际重大外交事务的重要参与者，削弱西方孤立莫斯科的效果。 美国前总统奥巴马（Barack Obama）政府时期的国务院高级官员丹尼·罗素（Danny Russel）向Euronews表示，普京是最有可能从三方会谈中获益的领袖，即使三方未能达成协议，只要普京能与特朗普及习近平同场亮相，已可向外界展示俄罗斯仍是国际重大外交事务的重要参与者，削弱西方孤立莫斯科的效果。 俄罗斯方面也明显积极推动会面。他形容，这将是普京的一次“外交上的重大胜利”。 莫斯科政治分析人士亚历山大·布拉特斯基（Alexander Bratersky）接受半岛电视台访问时指出，三方会谈本身已足以让俄罗斯取得政治宣传成果。俄罗斯官员曾将这类会谈比作1945年的雅尔塔会议，暗示大国领袖可共同塑造战后国际秩序。布拉特斯基认为，普京与特朗普及习近平同坐谈判桌，有助塑造俄罗斯参与决定欧洲未来安全架构的形象。他说：“单是举行这场会议，本身就是一项成功。普京将能够在国内将此事作为成果宣传。” 特朗普方面则希望借会谈展示其处理国际重大问题的能力。伦敦城市圣乔治大学国际政治学教授因德吉特·帕马尔（Inderjeet Parmar）认为，特朗普希望透过与另外两个大国领袖直接接触，塑造自己是不可或缺的协议促成者，并展示美国仍掌握国际主导权，即使会谈实际内容有限。 中国的考量则有所不同。美国智库史汀生中心（Stimson Center）中国项目主任孙韵指出，北京希望取得会谈带来的外交形象效益，却不愿承担额外成本。她说：“中国想要的是形象，而不是成本。” 特朗普预计这次访华将是他今年第三次与习近平会面。美中两国目前维持脆弱的贸易休战安排，协议预计于明年1月届满。中国今年主办APEC领导人非正式会议，成员包括美国及俄罗斯。 分析人士也关注，三方会谈可能令美国的欧洲及亚洲盟友被边缘化。帕马尔指出，二战后美国通常会先与盟友协调，再与俄罗斯或中国处理重大外交议题，若三国领袖绕过盟友直接讨论国际安全及经济安排，将反映美国外交模式出现转变。他说：“一场独立进行的三方会谈，可能将这些盟友视为次要角色，仿佛他们的利益可以在事后才处理。” 美国智库民主防卫基金会（Foundation for Defense of Democracies）中国项目高级主任克雷格·辛格尔顿（Craig Singleton）则认为，会谈可能最终只是一场让普京与美中领袖同框的拍照活动。他指出：“场面可能具有历史意义，却未必能产生任何特别重大的实际成果。”

title: (FRA獨家）特習會前北京醞釀五項貿易要求 涉關稅芯片及投資
summary: 特朗普與習近平計劃在APEC高峰會上進行今年第三次會唔。消息人士指出，中方醞釀提出五項貿易訴求，包括關稅、農產品採購、先進芯片及設備出口限制等。 (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP) 美國中期選舉之後，亞太經合組織（APEC）領導人非正式會議將於本月18日至19日在深圳舉行，美國總統特朗普預計與中國國家主席習近平在會議期間舉行今年第三次會面。 北京一位外貿部門人士向本臺透露，中方醞釀的五項貿易訴求涉及關稅、農產品採購、先進芯片及設備出口限制、中國企業赴美投
content: 特朗普與習近平計劃在APEC高峰會上進行今年第三次會唔。消息人士指出，中方醞釀提出五項貿易訴求，包括關稅、農產品採購、先進芯片及設備出口限制等。 (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP) 美國中期選舉之後，亞太經合組織（APEC）領導人非正式會議將於本月18日至19日在深圳舉行，美國總統特朗普預計與中國國家主席習近平在會議期間舉行今年第三次會面。 北京一位外貿部門人士向本臺透露，中方醞釀的五項貿易訴求涉及關稅、農產品採購、先進芯片及設備出口限制、中國企業赴美投資，以及跨境合規與多邊規則。其中，中方要求美方取消全部對華加徵關稅，落實農產品貿易便利化及關稅減讓安排，放寬先進芯片出口限制，併為中國企業赴美投資提供非歧視的營商環境。 北京擬要求取消對華加徵關稅 另一位不願公開身份和職務的人士說：“中方將要求美方徹底取消全部對華加徵關稅，還會提出以市場化原則積極擴大自美農產品進口，但前提是美方必須營造相應的貿易便利化條件，並切實給予關稅減讓。” 他還表示：“中方還要求美方停止對中國科技企業的無理打壓，停止將經貿科技問題泛安全化，並放寬相關先進芯片及設備的出口限制。” 上週四（5日），中國商務部發言人黃玲表示，中方對擴大采購美國農產品持開放態度，但前提是雙方達成的各涉及300億美元商品的對等降稅安排落實。她希望美方與中方共同降低關稅、減少非關稅壁壘及擴大市場準入。路透社報道，這項涉及雙方合計600億美元商品的降稅安排尚未最終落實。 中國外交部本週六發佈的消息顯示，中美經貿中方牽頭人、國務院副總理何立峰於本週五（6日）晚與美國財政部長貝森特、貿易代表格里爾舉行視頻通話，討論落實兩國元首北京和華盛頓會晤共識及經貿磋商成果。 另一位接近中國商務部的人士稱，中方正在考慮要求美方為中國電動車、電池及能源設備等企業赴美投資提供非歧視的營商環境。相關要求涉及中國企業在美國的市場準入、投資審查及經營條件。 習近平於2026年9月23日至25日對美國進行國事訪問期間，與特朗普就經貿問題達成多項共識，包括對雙方各約300億美元非敏感商品給予更優惠的關稅待遇，以及推進雙邊貿易和投資磋商機制。雙方還將此前達成的貿易休戰安排延長至2027年1月。相關關稅減讓措施尚未最終落實。 學者：中期選舉改變中美談判氣氛 研究中美關係的學者姚賦（化名）接受採訪時表示，在美國中期選舉改變美國政治格局之後，深圳APEC峰會期間的中美會晤氣氛也發生變化：“面對受到國會制約的特朗普，習肯定將利用特朗普剩下兩年執政，最大化習或中國的利益，包括貿易戰和臺灣問題等，並且以既定的所謂三巨頭峰會滿足特的虛榮心，製造其權力幻想。相信，習會趁機要求特在關稅、芯片等經貿問題上讓步，取消高關稅。” 姚賦進一步表示：“不過，是否達成合作成果仍然決定於特朗普本人能否說服習暫停對伊朗援助。畢竟關稅問題相比美伊戰爭，後者對特更為重要。目前局勢既有利於中方，看起來，習只要稍微在伊朗問題做出輕微讓步，便可從特朗普處大幅改善中美貿易關係和談判。” 資深評論人士蔡慎坤對本臺表示，美國中期選舉後，特朗普受到國會制約，北京可能調整對美談判策略。他說：“川普有可能不再堅持過去那麼強硬的貿易政策。因為他知道如果再堅持，中方會繼續的拖延，去年他們在釜山達成的協議現在已經不了了之，中國實際上一直在觀察，也在等待美國中期選舉。因為中期選舉川普輸了之後，很多制衡政策使得他很難發力了。” 談及臺灣問題，蔡慎坤錶示，北京希望特朗普在反對臺獨問題上作出表態，但美國兩黨在臺灣問題上的立場接近，特朗普讓步的空間有限。他認為，北京近期對臺灣採取軍事行動的可能性不大，2028年之後的政治變化可能影響臺海局勢。 對於中美俄三國領導人是否在深圳舉行會談，北京一位知情人士表示，中方目前對烏克蘭問題關注有限，更重視解決中美貿易摩擦及美國對臺軍售問題。他說：“今天已經8號了，還沒聽說特朗普、普京和習近平舉行三國元首會談已進入議事日程。” 伊朗問題成會談進展風向標 伊朗問題也是判斷中美高層會談能否取得進展的其中一個風向標。姚賦分析稱，北京在伊朗問題上的立場可能影響特朗普對華貿易談判的考慮。

title: 黄仁勋婚外情牵出间谍疑云：美中媒体如何讲述同一个故事？
summary: 资料照片：英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋在北京中国国际供应链博览会开幕式后，被媒体包围。(2025年7月16日) 华盛顿 — 英伟达(Nvidia)首席执行官黄仁勋承认婚外情，引发美国和中国舆论关注。不过，与一般的企业高管私人生活丑闻不同，这起事件还牵涉有关中国情报活动的指控，以及美国超级智能(通常称人工智能或AI)芯片产业面临的国家安全问题。 美国主流媒体的报道主要围绕黄仁勋与一名被怀疑可能与中国情报机构有关的女性有婚外情，并探讨这段关系是否可能涉及商业机密泄露，甚至危及美国国家安
content: 资料照片：英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋在北京中国国际供应链博览会开幕式后，被媒体包围。(2025年7月16日) 华盛顿 — 英伟达(Nvidia)首席执行官黄仁勋承认婚外情，引发美国和中国舆论关注。不过，与一般的企业高管私人生活丑闻不同，这起事件还牵涉有关中国情报活动的指控，以及美国超级智能(通常称人工智能或AI)芯片产业面临的国家安全问题。 美国主流媒体的报道主要围绕黄仁勋与一名被怀疑可能与中国情报机构有关的女性有婚外情，并探讨这段关系是否可能涉及商业机密泄露，甚至危及美国国家安全。 中国官方媒体则采取了明显不同的报道角度。它们提及黄仁勋的婚外情，但着重质疑有关中国间谍活动的说法，指责西方媒体借此炒作中国威胁论，甚至可能试图破坏美中关系。 美媒：从私人关系延伸到国家安全 美国《纽约时报》、《华尔街日报》以及其他西方媒体的报道，将这起事件置于美国与中国围绕超级智能技术展开竞争的大背景下。 相关报道指出，与黄仁勋有关系的女性黄乐(Alice Huang)据称与一家总部位于新加坡的数据中心企业超速国际(Megaspeed International)有关联。这家公司涉及英伟达先进超级智能芯片的商业活动，因此引起美国方面的关注。 《纽约时报》报道说，美国情报部门怀疑黄乐可能与中国情报机构存在联系，并向北京提供过信息。不过，这些指控目前尚未通过公开的司法程序得到证实。 《华尔街日报》星期一(11月9日)以时间线方式，详细报道从与黄乐有关的Megaspeed于2023年从一家中国公司分拆成立开始，回顾黄仁勋与黄乐在2024年、2025年同场出现，以及美国商务部随后调查Megaspeed是否将英伟达先进芯片转运至中国。 报道还梳理了特朗普政府对英伟达对华出口政策的讨论，以及美国情报部门在2026年春季向政府高层传阅机密备忘录的说法。到了11月8日，黄仁勋承认对妻子不忠，英伟达董事会随即启动独立调查。 黄仁勋事件之所以引人关注，与英伟达在美国科技产业和国家安全领域的重要地位密切相关。 作为全球领先的超级智能芯片制造商，英伟达不仅是美国科技产业的重要企业，也处于华盛顿对华高科技出口管制政策争论的中心。 黄仁勋过去多次公开反对过度限制美国企业向中国市场销售先进芯片，认为过于严厉的出口限制可能削弱美国企业的竞争力，同时推动中国加快发展自己的半导体产业。 目前没有公开证据证明黄仁勋明知对方从事情报活动，也没有确凿证据表明英伟达的商业机密已经因此泄露。 中国官方媒体：质疑间谍指控，强调政治动机 中国官方媒体对这起事件的报道呈现出明显不同的侧重点，主要通过否认和质疑间谍指控，批评美国媒体的报道方式及其背后的政治动机。 中国官媒《环球时报》将事件与当前美中关系联系起来，质疑有关指控出现的时机，认为有关报道可能意在制造美中之间的对立。 《环球时报》星期一发布题为《黄仁勋出轨，还能扯上中国？》的快评，称这一事件“让美国媒体为之疯狂”，并批评《纽约时报》有关黄仁勋婚外情对象可能是中国间谍的报道捕风捉影。 《环球时报》写道：“仅仅是几张有东方面孔的照片、英伟达此前推动放宽对华贸易限制的行动，在其中加入了所谓“知情人士”的话和媒体的“怀疑”，就足以将事情添油加醋为“中国女间谍渗透美国芯片公司”。向来自诩“客观”的美国媒体正是这样生产故事的。” 环球之后说，在美中关系趋于缓和之际，出现此类新闻，是有些人“在背后放冷枪”。 这篇评论随后被凤凰网、新浪、网易、腾讯等多家中国媒体转载，使其观点在中国网络媒体上得到进一步传播。 与美国媒体相比，这些报道较少深入讨论美国情报部门提出的具体疑点，也没有将相关情报指控作为报道的主要调查方向。报道的重点更多放在质疑美国媒体的消息来源、证据基础以及报道动机上。 中国外交部发言人郭嘉昆星期一在回应有关报道时，也否认中国从事相关间谍活动，称“所谓‘中国间谍’的论调纯属捕风捉影，污蔑抹黑。” 中国社交媒体：对婚外情的关注不亚于间谍疑云 中国社交媒体上的讨论则呈现出更加多元的面貌。 微博上，部分网民对黄仁勋的私人生活表示惊讶或失望。黄仁勋长期以来在中国科技界和商业界拥有较高知名度，不少中国公众将他视为华人科技企业家的代表人物。 在小红书上，除了讨论黄仁勋的婚外情及其可能涉及的间谍疑云，也有不少网友关注事件对英伟达股价的影响。 星期一早间，英伟达股价一度下跌超过8%，引发投资者讨论。有网友调侃说：“他犯的错，我买单。” 这些讨论显示，对不少中国网民来说，黄仁勋的私人生活、公众形象以及英伟达的市场表现，都是这起事件值得关注的方面。相比之下，间谍指控并非所有讨论的中心。

title: 英伟达股价再次下滑，CEO黄仁勋面临诉讼及FBI调查
summary: 在华盛顿美国和平研究所举行的一场活动中，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋在唐纳德·特朗普总统发言时倾听。(2026年10月8日) 英伟达(Nvidia)股价星期二(11月10日)连续第二天走低，这家位于美国的半导体公司首席执行官黄仁勋(Jensen Huang)同时面临股东诉讼，并承受着来自国会日益增长的压力。 此次抛售的前一天，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)说，联邦调查局(FBI)正在调查黄仁勋与女商人黄乐(Alice Huang)之间的关系；美国情报部门认定，这
content: 在华盛顿美国和平研究所举行的一场活动中，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋在唐纳德·特朗普总统发言时倾听。(2026年10月8日) 英伟达(Nvidia)股价星期二(11月10日)连续第二天走低，这家位于美国的半导体公司首席执行官黄仁勋(Jensen Huang)同时面临股东诉讼，并承受着来自国会日益增长的压力。 此次抛售的前一天，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)说，联邦调查局(FBI)正在调查黄仁勋与女商人黄乐(Alice Huang)之间的关系；美国情报部门认定，这名女商人是在为中国搜集情报。 英伟达董事会于星期日启动了独立审查，原因是有报道指黄仁勋成为外国情报机构的目标。黄仁勋在发给员工的一则信息中承认自己曾有不忠行为，但未透露女方身份。 特朗普与黄仁勋通话 英伟达股价在星期二上午交易时段下跌了5.3%。星期一收盘时，该股下跌了4.3%，导致公司市值缩水约1900亿美元。 特朗普在星期一的白宫简报会上说，他曾致电黄仁勋，询问其近况。 特朗普说，“我问了他那个问题：‘你知不知道她是间谍？’他说‘我完全不知道她是间谍。’我确实相信他，”“我知道联邦调查局正在调查此事，”“我认为他会没事的。” 特朗普将于下星期前往中国深圳参加亚太经合组织峰会，届时他预计将与中国国家主席习近平会晤。当被问及是否会向习提及此事时，特朗普说，“不，我想不会。我是说，也许吧。我相信习近平主席会问起这件事的。” 中国外交部发言人郭嘉昆星期二在北京拒绝表明习近平是否会提出这一问题。他仅表示，双方正在就两国领导人今年的会晤安排进行讨论。中方已否认了有关间谍指控。 投资人诉讼 散户投资者马克·基斯滕马赫(Mark Kistenmacher)星期一在加利福尼亚州圣何塞的联邦法院对英伟达及黄仁勋提起诉讼；他在一份拟议的集体诉讼中指控他们欺骗了股东。根据起诉书，英伟达隐瞒了相关事宜，并对其与Megaspeed公司之间的往来情况进行了失实陈述；Megaspeed是一家位于新加坡的企业，黄乐曾在此担任高管。诉讼文件指称，此举使英伟达的声誉和业务面临“重大风险”。 原告要求由陪审团审理此案，并寻求损害赔偿，但未明确具体金额。诉讼涵盖10月9日至11月8日期间买入英伟达股票的股东。英伟达未立即就此诉讼置评。 议员们要求给出答复 众议院民主党领袖哈基姆·杰弗里斯(Hakeem Jeffries)星期一说，“显然，国会需要更多信息。”杰弗里斯说。当天在中央情报局局长约翰·拉特克利夫(John Ratcliffe)和国家情报总监杰伊·克莱顿(Jay Clayton)参加的机密简报会上，伊朗问题占据了主导地位，英伟达只是被顺带提及。 马萨诸塞州民主党参议员伊丽莎白·沃伦(Elizabeth Warren)和印第安纳州共和党参议员吉姆·班克斯(Jim Banks)星期一在一份联合声明中说，这一事件使国家安全方面的担忧“变得更加紧迫”。他们敦促国会将《人工智能监管法案》(AI Overwatch Act)这个让国会能够监督最先进芯片出口的法案，纳入年度国防法案。 来自特拉瓦州的民主党参议员克里斯·库恩斯(Chris Coons)在X上写道，他正在“推动对黄仁勋及英伟达展开调查，以确定我们的国家安全是否受到了损害。”

title: AIT and TECRO Strengthen U.S.-Taiwan Partnership Through New Taiwan Fellowship Program
zh_title: AIT 和 TECRO 通过新的台湾奖学金计划加强美台伙伴关系
summary: AIT 与 TECRO 通过新台湾奖学金计划加强美台伙伴关系 PR-2631 2026 年 11 月 11 日 AIT 与 TECRO 通过新台湾奖学金计划加强美台伙伴关系 2026 年 11 月 10 日，美国在台协会 (AIT) 华盛顿常务董事 Ingrid Larson 与台北驻美国经济文化代表处 (TECRO) 代表 Alexander Tah-Ray Yui 签署了一份建立台湾奖学金计划（TFP）的谅解备忘录（MOU）。 《台湾联谊法》获得国会通过并签署成为法律
content:
AIT 和 TECRO 通过新的台湾奖学金计划加强美国与台湾的伙伴关系 PR-2631 2026 年 11 月 11 日 AIT 和 TECRO 通过新的台湾奖学金计划加强美国与台湾的伙伴关系 2026 年 11 月 10 日，美国在台协会 (AIT) 华盛顿董事总经理 Ingrid Larson 和台北驻美国经济文化代表处 (TECRO) 代表 Alexander Tah-Ray Yui 签署了一份建立台湾奖学金计划（TFP）的谅解备忘录（MOU）。 《台湾奖学金法案》在两党广泛支持下获得国会通过并签署成为法律。今天，AIT 和 TECRO 签署了谅解备忘录，并与国务院教育和文化事务局协调，启动了该计划的实施。该计划的主要目标是扩大和加强美台伙伴关系，并加强美国官员在台湾和海峡两岸问题上的专业知识。 TFP 将在台湾各地建立一批具有语言技能、文化知识和持久工作关系的联邦专业人士。根据该奖学金计划，美国联邦雇员将花费长达一年的时间进行强化普通话培训和地区研究。培训完成后，研究员预计将在台湾议会办公室、部委、其他机构或办公室或台湾公共部门以外的组织工作最长一年。
国会议员以及美国国务院、TECRO 和 AIT 的代表出席了在弗吉尼亚州阿灵顿举行的签字仪式，与会者称赞该计划在加强美台伙伴关系和建立美国政府在台湾问题上的专业知识方面所发挥的作用。美国在台协会董事总经理英格丽·拉尔森 (Ingrid Larson) 表示：“TFP 反映了两党对美台关系的大力支持以及对以民间关系为核心的共同承诺。” 《AIT 和 TECRO 通过新台湾奖学金计划加强美台伙伴关系》一文首先发表在美国在台协会上。

【原文 English Original】
AIT and TECRO Strengthen U.S.-Taiwan Partnership Through New Taiwan Fellowship Program PR-2631 November 11, 2026 AIT and TECRO Strengthen U.S.-Taiwan Partnership Through New Taiwan Fellowship Program   On November 10, 2026, American Institute in Taiwan (AIT) Washington Managing Director Ingrid Larson and the Taipei Economic and Cultural Representative Office in the United States (TECRO) Representative Alexander Tah-Ray Yui signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) to establish the Taiwan Fellowship Program (TFP).   The Taiwan Fellowship Act was passed by Congress and signed into law with broad bipartisan support. Today’s signing of the MOU between AIT and TECRO initiates the program’s implementation, in coordination with the Department of State’s Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs. The main objectives of the Program are to expand and strengthen the U.S.-Taiwan partnership, as well as strengthen U.S. officials’ expertise regarding Taiwan and cross-Strait issues. TFP will build a group of federal professionals with language skills, cultural knowledge, and lasting working relationships across Taiwan.   Under the fellowship program, U.S. federal employees will spend up to one year in intensive Mandarin language training and area studies. Upon completion of training, the Fellows are expected to work, for up to one year, in Taiwan parliamentary offices, ministries, other agencies or offices, or organizations outside the public sector in Taiwan.   Members of Congress and representatives from the U.S. Department of State, TECRO, and AIT attended the signing ceremony in Arlington, Virginia, where attendees praised the program’s role in strengthening the U.S.-Taiwan partnership and building U.S. government expertise on Taiwan.   “TFP reflects strong bipartisan support for the U.S.-Taiwan relationship and a shared commitment to the people-to-people ties at its core,” said AIT Managing Director Ingrid Larson. The post AIT and TECRO Strengthen U.S.-Taiwan Partnership Through New Taiwan Fellowship Program appeared first on American Institute in Taiwan .

title: F-16V vs F-16C Block 70/72: Understanding The Differences Between The Latest Viper Variants
zh_title: F-16V 与 F-16C Block 70/72：了解最新 Viper 变体之间的差异
summary: 尽管经常互换使用，F-16V 和 F-16C Block 70/72 名称描述了毒蛇进化的两个方面，升级飞机和新建飞机之间存在重要区别。 F-16 战隼的最新发展成为近几个月多条新闻的焦点，突显了该机在首次飞行后 50 多年里如何继续发展。从交付客户的新生产战斗机到现有机队的广泛现代化计划，最新进展表明第四代战斗机仍然是战斗机的重要组成部分。
content:
尽管经常互换使用，F-16V 和 F-16C Block 70/72 名称描述了毒蛇进化的两个方面，升级飞机和新建飞机之间存在重要区别。 F-16 战隼的最新发展成为近几个月多条新闻的焦点，突显了该机在首次飞行后 50 多年里如何继续发展。从交付客户的新生产战斗机到现有机队的广泛现代化计划，最新进展表明第四代战斗机仍然是众多空军未来计划的重要组成部分。 10 月，台湾收到了首批两架新制造的 F-16C Block 70 战斗机，这是拖延已久的 66 架飞机订单的一部分。此次交付标志着一个重要的里程碑，这些喷气式飞机补充了升级为 F-16V 配置的岛上现有机队。第二批飞机已于 11 月初交付，同时飞机的训练仍在美国亚利桑那州图森市的莫里斯空军国民警卫队基地继续进行。航空摄影师 Thomas Backus (@machtwoimages) 拍摄了其中两个机身，并与我们分享了这些图像。同样在10月，洛克希德·马丁公司宣布摩洛哥首架F-16D Block 72首飞，这也是第一架新制造的Block 72喷气式飞机。摩洛哥还在推行并行现代化工作，将 23 架现有 F-16C/D Block 52 飞机升级为 F-16V 配置。
说到现代化的“毒蛇”战斗机，希腊于 9 月接收了第 60 架 F-16V，作为该计划的一部分，该计划将首先将 84 架 F-16 Block 52+ 和 Block 52+ Advanced 升级到新配置，然后是 38 架较旧的 Block 50。与此同时，洛克希德·马丁公司向美国空军和 F-16C/D Block 推销了一款基于 Block 70 的变体，称为 F-16G。 70/72 给乌克兰空军。 Visualizza questo post su Instagram                         Un post condiviso da Thomas “Taj” Backus (@machtwoimages) 这些进展说明了运营商投资“战隼”的不同方式。然而，它们也重新引起了人们对即使是航空爱好者也可能感到困惑的术语的关注：F-16V、F-16C/D、Block 70 和 Block 72。虽然这些名称有时可以互换使用，但它们并不意味着同一件事。了解每个名称的含义对于区分新制造的 F-16C/D Block 70/72 和升级到 F-16V 配置的旧版 F-16 至关重要。了解名称 F-16V（其中“V”代表 F-16 的昵称“毒蛇”）由洛克希德·马丁公司推出，作为现有“战隼”战斗机的现代化套件。 F-16V 于 2012 年宣布并于 2015 年首飞，旨在使早期的 F-16 改型达到更先进的技术标准，而不需要运营商购买全新的飞机。
该套件对飞机的雷达、任务计算机、驾驶舱显示器和航空电子设备架构进行了重大改进。这些更改随后被纳入新制造飞机的 Block 70/72 生产配置中。 Block 名称标识了 F-16 的特定渐进生产标准，从 F-16A Block 1 开始。F-16C 和 F-16D 名称（类似于 F-16A 和 B，以及 F-16E 和 F）分别标识飞机的单座和两座变体。 ROCAF F-16V 准备快速反应啤酒

【原文 English Original】
Although often used interchangeably, the F-16V and the F-16C Block 70/72 designations describe two sides of the Viper’s evolution, with important differences between upgraded and newly built aircraft. The F-16 Fighting Falcon’s latest evolution has been at the center of several news in recent months, highlighting how the aircraft continues to evolve more than five decades after its first flight. From new-production fighters reaching customers to extensive modernization programs for existing fleets, the latest developments show that the fourth-generation fighter remains an important component of numerous air forces’ future plans. In October, Taiwan received its first two newly manufactured F-16C Block 70 fighters , part of a long-delayed order for 66 aircraft. The delivery marked an important milestone, with these jets complementing the island’s existing fleet upgraded to the F-16V configuration. A second batch was delivered in early November, while training on the aircraft continues in the U.S. at Morris Air National Guard Base in Tucson, Arizona. Aviation photographer Thomas Backus ( @machtwoimages ) photographed two of the airframes and kindly shared the images with us. Also in October, Lockheed Martin announced the maiden flight of Morocco’s first F-16D Block 72, which is also the first newly manufactured Block 72 jet . Morocco is also pursuing a parallel modernization effort, upgrading 23 existing F-16C/D Block 52 aircraft to the F-16V configuration. Speaking of modernized Vipers, in September, Greece received its 60th F-16V, as part of a program which will first see 84 F-16s Block 52+ and Block 52+ Advanced upgraded to the new configuration, followed by 38 older Block 50s. Meanwhile, Lockheed Martin pitched a Block 70-based variant called F-16G to the U.S. Air Force and the F-16C/D Block 70/72 to the Ukrainian Air Force.             Visualizza questo post su Instagram                         Un post condiviso da Thomas “Taj” Backus (@machtwoimages) These developments illustrate the different ways in which operators are investing in the Fighting Falcon. However, they have also brought renewed attention to a terminology that can be confusing even for aviation enthusiasts: F-16V, F-16C/D, Block 70 and Block 72. Although these designations are sometimes used interchangeably, they do not mean the same thing. Understanding what each designation means is essential to distinguish a newly manufactured F-16C/D Block 70/72 from an older F-16 upgraded to the F-16V configuration . Understanding the designations The F-16V, with the ‘V’ standing for the F-16’s nickname Viper, was introduced by Lockheed Martin as a modernization package for existing Fighting Falcons. Announced in 2012 and first flying in 2015 , the F-16V was intended to bring earlier F-16 variants up to a more advanced technological standard without requiring operators to purchase entirely new aircraft. The package introduced significant improvements to the aircraft’s radar, mission computers, cockpit displays and avionics architecture. These changes were subsequently incorporated into the Block 70/72 production configuration for newly manufactured aircraft. The Block designation identifies a particular progressive production standard of the F-16, starting with the F-16A Block 1. The F-16C and F-16D designations (similarly to the F-16A and B, and the F-16E and F ) identify the aircraft single-seat and two-seat variants, respectively. A ROCAF F-16V prepares for a Quick Reaction Alert mission during a combat readiness exercise in 2022. | Source: CNA Consequently, an F-16C Block 70/72 is a single-seat, newly manufactured Fighting Falcon built to the latest production standard, while an F-16D Block 70/72 is its two-seat counterpart. The Block 70 and 72 designations identify different engine configurations, which will be discussed later. An existing F-16C or F-16D (or, in Taiwan’s case, F-16A or F-16B ) modernized to the F-16V standard retains its original airframe and powerplant. However, many of its systems are brought up to a configuration comparable to the Block 70/72 production aircraft, with few differences. The similarities: radar and avionic upgrades Among the new systems installed om both the modernized F-16V and the newly manufactured Block 70/72 we can find the  APG-83 AESA  (Active Electronically Scanned Array) radar, a new Center Pedestal Display (CPD), the AN/APX-126 Advanced IFF (Identification Friend or Foe), Link 16 datalink, full NVIS (Night Vision Imaging System) and JHCMS II (Joint Helmet-Mounted Cueing System II) compatibility, a new Embedded GPS/INS (EGI), a modern commercial off-the-shelf (COTS)-based avionics subsystem, a high-volume, high-speed data bus and the  Automatic Ground Collision Avoidance System (Auto GCAS). The radar, built by Northrop Grumman as the Scalable Agile Beam Radar (SABR), is undoubtedly one of the most important features. Notably, this radar is designed to fit the F-16 with no structural, power or cooling modifications, and is also being installed on U.S. Air Force F-16s as part of the ongoing upgrades . This AESA radar represents a significant improvement over the mechanically scanned AN/APG-66 and AN/APG-68 radars fitted to earlier F-16 variants. Unlike mechanically scanned radars, which rely on a moving antenna to direct the radar beam, an AESA uses multiple transmit/receive modules to electronically steer the beam. Two Republic of China Air Force (ROCAF) F-16C Block 70 jets on the ground at Morris Air National Guard Base in Tucson, Arizona. | Source: Thomas Backus machtwoimages The new radar enables the F-16 to detect, track and identify a greater number of targets (reportedly more than 20 at the same time) faster and at longer ranges while providing all-weather, high-resolution Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) mapping. The system also integrated a robust electronic protection to operate in hostile electronic environments. The radar is complemented by an upgraded Modular Mission Computer and a modernized avionics architecture. This is designed to process the increased volume of information generated by the new sensors and provide pilots with a more comprehensive tactical picture. The cockpit has also received substantial improvements, with one of the most recognizable additions being the Center Pedestal Display (CPD). The CPS is a high-resolution, 6-by-8-inch color display installed in the center of the instrument panel instead of the older analog gauges, providing access to radar information, targeting pod imagery, digital maps and other tactical data, complementing the existing Multi-Function Displays (MFD). The newly manufactured aircraft also include new digital standby attitude indicator, engine and fuel gauges, as well as a new Integrated Control Panel (ICP) which includes the Data Entry Display (DED). On the other hand, the F-16V retains the original standby attitude indicator, engine and fuel gauges, and ICP, with the DED remaining in the original position. The differences: new and life-extended airframe Perhaps the most important distinction between a newly manufactured Block 70 and an older F-16 upgraded to the F-16V standard concerns the airframe itself. The Block 70/72 features a structural service life of 12,000 flight hours, while the F-16V features an airframe which already accumulated a number of flight hours and underwent a Service Life Extension Program (SLEP) during the upgrade . A Republic of China Air Force (ROCAF) F-16C Block 70 returns from a training sortie at Morris Air National Guard Base in Tucson, Arizona. | Source: Thomas Backus machtwoimages The Block 70/72’s structural service life is more than 50% greater than that of previous production F-16s, according to Lockheed Martin. This was achieved through structural improvements incorporated during manufacturing, allowing the aircraft to remain in service for several decades without requiring the same extensive structural interventions that older airframes may eventually need. This distinction is particularly important when comparing the two configurations. In fact, although an upgraded F-16V may offer similar avionics and mission capabilities to a Block 70/72, the latter starts from zero flight hours since it is newly manufactured, while the former’s service life depends on the original aircraft’s condition and operational history. Engine and external configuration The Block 70 and Block 72 designations, as mentioned earlier, identify different engine configurations. The Block 70 is powered by the General Electric F110-GE-129D turbofan , while the Block 72 uses the Pratt & Whitney F100-PW-229 engine. Both engines belong to established families already used by previous F-16 variants, but the choice of powerplant depends on the customer’s requirements and existing logistics infrastructure. The use of the Block x0/x2 designation goes back to the early 1980s, when it was first used for the F-16C/D Block 30 and Block 32 aircraft. The F-16’s initial variants – from the A/B Block 1 to the C/D Block 25 – were powered by the Pratt & Whitney F100-PW-200 turbofan, followed by the upgraded F100-PW-220 turbofan. However, in 1984, the U.S. Air Force decided to adopt both P&W and GE engines under the Alternative Fighter Engine (AFE) program. The F-16C/D Block 30/32 thus included a common engine bay, able to accept either powerplant. However, that was not the only modification required for the different engine. In fact, with GE’s F110 providing more thrust and thus requiring a larger airflow, the air inlet had to be enlarged. This led to the larger inlet becoming the standard for F110-powered F-16s, which were referred to as “ Big-mouths,” while the F100-powered F-16s retained the original smaller inlet as the larger one would be detrimental to the flight performance.

title: 美国海军退伍军人秦伟平正式宣布参选Katy ISD学区董事：从军旅服役到教育公共治理，提出SMART五大教育纲领
summary: 纵览中国｜美国德克萨斯州Katy市｜2026年11月11日 美国海军退伍军人、美国邮政服务（USPS）职业雇员、公共管理硕士（MPA）候选人秦伟平（Weiping “George” Qin）于2026年11月11日美国退伍军人节正式宣布参选美国德克萨斯州Katy独立学区（Katy Independent School District，简称Katy ISD）董事会第六选区（Position 6），计划参加2027年5月1日举行的学区董事会选举。 秦伟平通过其官方X（原Twit
content: 纵览中国｜美国德克萨斯州Katy市｜2026年11月11日 美国海军退伍军人、美国邮政服务（USPS）职业雇员、公共管理硕士（MPA）候选人秦伟平（Weiping “George” Qin）于2026年11月11日美国退伍军人节正式宣布参选美国德克萨斯州Katy独立学区（Katy Independent School District，简称Katy ISD）董事会第六选区（Position 6），计划参加2027年5月1日举行的学区董事会选举。 秦伟平通过其官方X（原Twitter）、Facebook及Substack等平台发布中英文正式竞选公告，并同步公布竞选团队新闻通稿及五大教育政策方向。他提出以 SMART Education Agenda（SMART教育纲领） 为核心的竞选框架，涵盖学生学业成就、学生支持、教师招聘与留任、财政管理，以及学区透明度和社区信任等议题。 秦伟平选择在退伍军人节宣布参选，将个人的海军服役经历与继续服务社会、参与地方教育公共事务的意愿联系起来。其竞选口号为： “Served Our Country. Defending Our Classrooms.” 中文表述为： “军旅报国，教育为民。” 此次公告标志着秦伟平此前持续进行的竞选筹备工作进入正式公开阶段，也使其个人经历、教育理念和地方公共治理主张开始集中呈现于公众面前。 一、退伍军人节宣布参选：公共服务从军旅延伸到社区 秦伟平在竞选公告中表示，公共服务不会随着军旅生涯的结束而终止，而是可以继续体现在对家庭、社区和下一代的责任与承诺之中。 据竞选团队提供的个人资料，秦伟平曾在美国海军服役，服役期间获得海军与海军陆战队成就奖章（Navy and Marine Corps Achievement Medal）以及军队杰出志愿服务奖章（Military Outstanding Volunteer Service Medal），以表彰其服役表现和志愿服务贡献。 在美国海军服役期间，他曾在舰艇供应部门工作，参与海军舰艇后勤保障任务，并取得航空作战专业资格（Enlisted Aviation Warfare Specialist，EAWS）和水面作战专业资格（Enlisted Surface Warfare Specialist，ESWS）。 这些经历构成了其个人介绍中关于军事训练、团队协作和公共服务的重要部分。 结束军旅服役后，秦伟平继续加入美国邮政服务系统（United States Postal Service，USPS），从事公共服务工作。 据竞选团队提供的资料，他曾在Katy邮局担任城市邮递员助理（City Carrier Assistant，CCA），负责邮件投递和当地社区服务。目前，他是USPS正式职业雇员，在Fulshear邮局担任邮政业务职员（Clerk）。 从海军后勤保障到邮政系统的日常运营，两段工作经历虽然属于不同领域，但都与公共服务和服务对象的实际需求密切相关。 秦伟平在竞选声明中表示，希望将海军服役期间形成的纪律意识、团队合作精神和责任担当，以及在联邦公共服务岗位上积累的工作经验，带入地方教育公共事务。 二、三个Katy ISD学生的父亲：从家长身份关注公共教育 除了军事和公共服务经历，秦伟平的另一个身份是Katy社区居民，也是三名正在Katy ISD就读学生的父亲。 对于当地家庭而言，学校教育质量、教师队伍稳定性、校园安全、特殊教育资源和学区财政安排，都是与日常生活密切相关的公共事务。 作为学生家长，秦伟平表示，他不仅关注自己孩子的教育环境，也希望学区能够关注整个社区不同家庭、不同学习需求以及不同学生群体的实际情况。 他的竞选公告强调，学区应该倾听家长意见，尊重教师和学校工作人员，合理使用纳税人的资金，并通过透明度和公共问责机制建立社区信任。 从其公开提出的政策方向来看，秦伟平希望将家长的实际体验与学区治理层面的讨论联系起来，使学生发展、教师支持和公共财政管理成为相互关联的议题。 三、从学生会主席到设立奖学金：教育经历与校园领导实践 秦伟平的教育背景和校园领导经历，也是此次竞选团队新闻通稿重点介绍的内容。 据竞选团队提供的履历资料，秦伟平曾就读于马里兰州哈福德社区大学（Harford Community College），并于2019年当选该校学生会（Student Government Association，SGA）主席。 2021年，他在该校设立了“秦伟平自由奖学金”（Weiping Qin Freedom Scholarship）。据竞选团队介绍，该奖学金旨在支持学生领袖以及具有军队服役经历的学生。 2023年，他获得哈福德社区大学颁发的杰出校友奖（Distinguished Alumni Award）。竞选团队将这一荣誉归因于其个人成就以及对学校和社区的贡献。 在高等教育方面，据其提供的个人履历，秦伟平先后获得哈福德社区大学工商管理副学士学位及会计证书，随后取得马里兰大学全球校区（University of Maryland Global Campus，UMGC）管理研究理学学士学位和工商管理硕士（MBA）学位。 目前，他正在金门大学（Golden Gate University，GGU）攻读公共管理硕士（Master of Public Administration，MPA）学位。 从学生会领导经历、奖学金设立，到继续学习工商管理和公共管理，秦伟平的教育背景涉及学生组织、商业管理和公共部门治理等多个领域。 对于一名地方学区董事候选人而言，这些经历也构成其公开介绍个人教育理念和公共管理兴趣的背景。至于如何将这些学习与实践经验转化为具体的学区政策，仍有待其在后续竞选活动中进一步阐述。 四、了解Katy ISD：近9.5万名学生、1.36万名教职员工的教育系统 要理解秦伟平此次竞选的公共事务背景，有必要先了解Katy ISD的规模，以及其董事会在当地教育体系中所承担的职责。 Katy ISD是美国德克萨斯州休斯敦西部地区的重要公立学区之一。根据德克萨斯州教育厅（Texas Education Agency，TEA）公布的2025—2026学年学区资料，截至2026年11月公布的最新统计，该学区共有 95,136名在校学生、78所学校 ，全职教职员工约13,601人，其中全职教师约6,934人。 这一规模意味着，Katy ISD不仅是一个服务近十万名学生的公共教育系统，也是当地规模较大的公共服务机构之一。其教育政策、财政预算和学校资源配置，直接关系到大量学生、家长、教师及社区居民。 从学生构成来看，TEA数据显示，2025—2026学年Katy ISD学生中，约43.3%属于经济条件相对困难群体，19.2%接受特殊教育服务，24.0%属于英语学习者（Emergent Bilingual Students）。 这些比例反映出学区内部学生需求具有多样性。不同学生在语言学习、特殊教育、学业支持和家庭资源方面可能面临不同情况，也使得教育资源分配和学生支持政策成为学区治理的重要议题。 TEA公布的同一学年资料还显示，Katy ISD的师生比例约为13.7名学生对应一名教师，教师平均年薪约为73,094美元。该学区在2025—2026学年的州级学区问责评级为B，得分88分（满分100分）。 从地理范围来看，根据Katy ISD官方网站介绍，学区覆盖面积约为181平方英里，服务范围涉及Harris、Fort Bend和Waller三个县。需要注意的是，Katy ISD的学区边界并不等同于Katy市的行政边界，其服务范围延伸至Katy市及周边多个社区。 因此，讨论Katy ISD的学生规模和公共服务范围时，应当以学区实际统计为依据，而不能简单将Katy市的人口数字等同于学区人口。 五、年度预算约14.8亿美元：教育资源与纳税人责任 Katy ISD的财政规模同样值得关注。 根据学区2026年8月24日公布的2026—2027财政年度预算信息，董事会批准了约 11.7亿美元的一般运营基金预算（General Operating Fund） 。加上食品服务及债务偿还等其他基金，学区年度总预算约为 14.8亿美元 。 学区公布的信息显示，约83%的预算支出用于学生教学、课堂运营和学生支持。这些资金涉及教师及学校工作人员薪酬、教学活动、学生服务和学校日常运行等重要领域。 与此同时，学区公布的2026—2027年度预算预计存在约2,570万美元的运营赤字。学区方面表示，过去三个已经审计的财政年度，虽然最初均采用赤字预算，但最终通过节约开支、控制实际支出及提高运营效率等措施，实现了年度预算平衡，并增加了基金余额。学区管理层预计2025—2026财政年度也有望延续这一趋势。 在税收方面，学区公布的2026—2027年度拟议综合税率为每100美元应税财产估值1.1171美元，与上一年度保持一致。该税率包括一般运营税率和债务偿还税率。 这些数字说明，学区董事会所涉及的并非单纯的教育理念讨论，还包括规模庞大的公共财政管理工作。 如何在保障教学质量、支持教师队伍、满足特殊教育需求、维护校园设施和控制纳税人负担之间取得平衡，是学区治理长期面对的议题。 这也与秦伟平此次提出的SMART教育纲领中的“R——Responsible Financial Management（负责任的财政管理）”以及“T——Transparency & Community Trust（透明度与社区信任）”两项政策方向直接相关。 六、Katy ISD董事会：七名民选成员共同承担学区治理职责 Katy ISD董事会（Board of Trustees）是学区的政策制定和公共监督机构，由七名董事组成。 根据Katy ISD官方网站，董事通过选举产生，每人任期三年，采取轮换选举方式。董事会成员不领取董事职务薪酬，候选人虽然以不同选区或席位参加选举，但当选后代表整个学区履行职责。 根据德克萨斯州教育厅对公立学区董事会职责的说明，以及Katy ISD公布的董事会制度，董事会主要负责： 制定学区政策和长期发展目标； 聘用、监督并评估学区总监（Superintendent）； 审议和批准年度预算及地方税率； 对学区财务、教育质量和整体管理进行监督； 通过正式董事会会议审议公共教育事务。 需要特别说明的是，学区董事并不直接负责每所学校的日常教学和行政管理。学校日常运营主要由学区总监及其管理团队负责，董事会则通过政策制定、预算批准、目标设定和管理监督履行职责。 此外，董事会作为一个集体机构作出正式决策，单独一名董事不能自行代表整个董事会作出决定。 这一制度安排意味着，学区董事并不是学校的日常行政管理人员，而是代表公众参与公共教育治理的民选代表。 对于即将参加Position 6选举的秦伟平而言，未来如果当选，其职责将不仅涉及自己所在选区的家庭，也将涉及整个Katy ISD学区的公共教育事务。 因此，学生学业表现、教师招聘与留任、特殊教育资源、学区预算、债务管理、学校设施规划以及家长参与机制，都属于与董事会职责密切相关的政策议题。 七、SMART教育纲领：五个方向回应学区治理议题 此次竞选公告最重要的政策内容，是秦伟平正式提出的SMART Education Agenda。 SMART由五个英文关键词的首字母组成，也是其竞选团队用来概括五大教育优先事项的整体框架。 S — Student Success & Academic Excellence 学生成就与学术卓越 秦伟平提出，应当巩固学生在阅读、数学及其他核心学科方面的基础，扩大STEM（科学、技术、工程与数学）教育机会，并提升学生在大学升学和职业发展方面的准备能力。 这一方向强调，学校教育不仅要关注学生是否完成课程，更应关注实际学习成果，以及学生在不同教育阶段所获得的发展机会。 M — Meaningful Support for Every Student 为每一位学生提供实质支持 这一部分特别关注具有不同学习需求的学生。 竞选团队提出的政策方向包括审视特殊教育服务与资源配置，加强对失读症（Dyslexia）和自闭症学生的支持，关注资优生（Gifted and Talented, G/T）项目，并进一步改善英语学习者（English Language Learners，ELL）的教育服务。 这一主张涉及学区资源分配、特殊教育服务和不同学生群体的教育机会。如何评估现有服务的覆盖程度、资源需求和实际成效，将是这一政策方向未来需要进一步讨论的内容。 A — Attract & Retain Great Educators 吸引并留住优秀教师 教师招聘和留任是秦伟平提出的第三项重点。 其竞选纲领提出，应审视教师招聘和留任机制，支持具有竞争力的教师薪酬，同时关注教师工作量、行政负担以及学校工作环境。 这一方向将教师队伍稳定性与学生教育质量联系起来，强调教师不仅需要专业能力，也需要获得适当的工作支持和职业尊重。 R — Responsible Financial Management 负责任的财政管理 在财政管理方面，秦伟平提出加强预算监督和财政信息透明度，审查学区债务及利息支出，并结合学生入学人数预测，合理评估学校建筑、设施和长期教育资源需求。 学区财政管理涉及教育服务质量、公共资金使用和纳税人利益。秦伟平提出的方向，重点在于预算监督、长期规划和资源配置之间的协调。 未来，这一纲领还需要进一步说明具体的预算审查方法、评估指标，以及如何在财政约束与教育需求之间取得平衡。 T — Transparency & Community Trust 透明度与社区信任 第五项政策重点是改善学区与社区之间的沟通。 秦伟平提出，应提高学区公共信息的透明度和可读性，鼓励家长及社区居民参与学区事务，加强公共问责，并推动开放、理性和相互尊重的公共讨论。 这一方向强调，学区治理不仅涉及董事会内部决策，也涉及家长、教师、学校工作人员和社区居民能否及时获得信息、表达意见并了解决策依据。 总体而言，SMART五大纲领将学生学业、教育公平、教师队伍、公共财政和社区参与纳入同一个政策框架，体现了秦伟平此次竞选所关注的主要治理领域。 八、2027年5月选举：Position 6与Position 7将列入选票 根据Katy ISD官方网站公布的信息，学区将于 2027年5月1日举行普通选举 ，董事会第六选区（Position 6）和第七选区（Position 7）将列入选票，选出的董事任期为三年。 官方公布的候选人申请时间为2027年1月13日至2027年2月12日下午5时。候选人需要按照学区公布的程序和德克萨斯州相关法律提交正式申请，并满足相应的参选资格要求。 因此，秦伟平此次宣布参选，属于正式公开宣布竞选意向和开展竞选活动的阶段，并不等同于已经完成正式候选人申请或取得选票资格。 Katy ISD官方网站的董事会资料页面目前列有七个董事席位，其中Position 6显示为空缺。该席位也将列入2027年5月选举。 随着选举临近，候选人将有机会进一步向社区介绍自己的教育理念、治理思路和具体政策方案。对于选民而言，了解不同候选人对学生发展、教师支持、财政管理和社区参与的具体主张，将是参与地方教育治理的重要一环。 九、从公共服务到地方教育：竞选主张仍有待社区检验 秦伟平在退伍军人节发布的声明中，将自己参选的原因概括为希望继续服务社区，为下一代创造更好的教育环境。 他在竞选团队发布的新闻通稿中表示： “对我而言，退伍军人节不仅是一个纪念的日子，更是一种精神的延续。军旅服役虽然有结束的一天，但服务社会的使命不应就此停止。我们可以继续以实际行动奉献社区，为下一代创造更加美好的未来。” 他还表示，作为美国海军退伍军人，自己曾有机会为国家服役；退役后继续通过美国邮政为公众服务；如今作为三名Katy ISD学生的父亲，希望通过参与学校发展、支持教师和保障学生成长机会，继续为社区作出贡献。 从其此次公布的竞选资料来看，秦伟平试图将三方面经历联系起来：军队服役所强调的纪律和责任、联邦公共服务岗位所涉及的日常运营，以及家庭作为学校教育直接参与者的实际体验。 但从竞选纲领走向学区治理，还需要将原则转化为具体政策。例如，如何衡量学生学业进步？如何确定特殊教育资源需求？怎样评估教师留任政策？如何在学校设施投资与财政可持续性之间取得平衡？又如何让家长和社区居民更有效地参与决策？ 这些问题不仅是候选人需要进一步回答的政策议题，也是选民在未来竞选过程中可以持续关注和比较的内容。 随着2027年5月选举临近，候选人将有更多机会向社区介绍各自的教育理念、治理思路和具体政策方案。秦伟平此次公布的SMART教育纲领，为其竞选确立了五个主要方向；这些主张能否形成更加明确、可执行和可评估的政策，将成为后续竞选讨论的重要部分。 秦伟平竞选信息 姓名： Weiping “George” Qin（秦伟平） 竞选职位： Katy ISD Board of Trustees, Position 6 选举日期： 2027年5月1日 竞选口号： Served Our Country. Defending Our Classrooms. 中文口号： 军旅报国，教育为民。 竞选纲领： SMART Education Agenda 官方竞选网站： https://weipingqintx.com/ 竞选联系邮箱： weipingqincampaign@gmail.com 秦伟平于2026年11月11日通过官方社交媒体发布中英文正式竞选公告，并邀请Katy ISD家长、教师、学校工作人员和社区居民关注其竞选活动，了解教育纲领并参与有关当地公共教育未来的讨论。 资料来源与说明： 本文根据秦伟平2026年11月11日公开发布的中英文正式竞选公告、竞选团队提供的媒体新闻通稿，以及以下公开资料整理： 德克萨斯州教育厅（TEA）Katy ISD 2025—2026学年学区资料。 Katy ISD 2026—2027财政年度预算公告。 Katy ISD董事会官方网站及董事会制度说明。 Katy ISD 2027年5月1日普通选举公告。 其中，个人服役经历、奖项、学历、奖学金及竞选主张依据竞选团队提供的材料表述；学区规模、财政预算、董事会制度及选举日期依据官方公开资料核对。 —— 纵览中国报道

title: Topco Scientific Establishes Dresden Hub, Makes SEMICON Europa Debut
zh_title: Topco Scientific 建立德累斯顿中心，SEMICON Europa 首次亮相
summary: 在《欧洲芯片法案》和半导体本土化制造趋势的推动下，欧洲对材料、设备和技术服务的需求日益受到关注。半导体产业综合服务商拓普科科技股份有限公司（TAIEX：5434）宣布，其德国子公司拓普科德国有限公司（TOPCO GERMANY）将首次参加11月10日至13日在德国慕尼黑展览中心举行的SEMICON Europa 2026，与台湾、日本的供应商合作伙伴一起展示其跨界合作。
content:
在《欧洲芯片法案》和半导体本土化制造趋势的推动下，欧洲对材料、设备和技术服务的需求日益受到关注。半导体产业综合服务商拓普科科技股份有限公司（TAIEX：5434）宣布，其德国子公司拓普科德国有限公司（TOPCO GERMANY）将首次参加11月10日至13日在德国慕尼黑展览中心举行的SEMICON Europa 2026，与台湾、日本供应商合作伙伴展示其跨境资源一体化和本地化服务能力。拓普科德国于2026年8月正式成立，将亮相台湾馆，展示涵盖工艺材料、特种化学品、扩散工艺清洗设备、关键零部件的一站式解决方案。这些解决方案旨在支持欧洲代工厂和汽车电子制造商的晶圆厂建设和生产需求。作为欧洲最大的半导体集群之一，德累斯顿是博世、英飞凌、恩智浦和格罗方德等主要半导体公司的所在地。随着世界领先的铸造厂在德国落户，TOPCO SCIENTIFIC 正在加速向欧洲市场的扩张。
该公司利用德累斯顿当地团队提供及时的材料供应和技术支持，将来自台湾、日本和其他市场的领先材料、设备和耗材供应商与欧洲客户联系起来。这种集成服务模式可帮助客户在半导体工厂不断扩张的情况下减轻供应链中断风险，并降低资质和入厂成本。对于关键的前端工艺材料，拓普科将在展会上展示日本供应商SHIN-ETSU POLYMER的12英寸晶圆载具解决方案，满足欧洲12英寸代工厂和集成器件制造商（IDM）严格的清洁度和自动化要求。其前开式统一盒 (FOUP) 具有抗静电保护和一体式结构，有助于缩短清洁和干燥周期，同时有效减少颗粒的产生。该公司还将展示符合 SEMI 标准的前开式运输箱 (FOSB)，并具有坚固的密封结构，可在长途国际运输过程中保护晶圆。为了满足先进半导体工艺的微缩要求，拓普科引进日本先进的前驱体材料，为高端薄膜沉积工艺提供全面的解决方案，包括化学气相沉积（CVD）和物理气相沉积（PVD）。
这些材料具有超高纯度和出色的热稳定性，有助于提高器件性能和产量，支持可靠的先进半导体制造。对于蚀刻和薄膜沉积工艺，TOPCO SCIENTIFIC 将展示使用 TAIWAN E&M SYSTEMS 的定制精密加工能力制造的关键组件。这些组件由石英、硅、陶瓷和碳化硅 (SiC) 制成，与主要半导体设备平台兼容。结合专门的抗等离子和耐磨涂层技术，它们有助于延长设备耗材的使用寿命，使客户能够提高产量，同时支持更可持续的制造。

【原文 English Original】
Driven by the European Chips Act and the trend toward localized semiconductor manufacturing, demand for materials, equipment, and technical services in Europe has attracted growing attention. TOPCO SCIENTIFIC Co., Ltd.
